findings.title: set_window_size / set_window_state(state='normal') ignore the requested bounds when the window is maximized, minimized or fullscreen
findings.scenario: await tab.maximize() (or minimize()/fullscreen()), then await tab.set_window_size(200, 100, 900, 700). For the normal state, set_window_state sends one Browser.setWindowBounds with windowState=normal plus left/top/width/height. When the window is not normal, Chrome only restores it and drops the geometry. The code handles the reverse case ('min, max, full can only be used when current state == NORMAL') but not this one. The window ends up at 0,0 1280x720 instead of 200,100 900x700, and no error is raised.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls maximize/minimize/fullscreen/medimize/set_window_size/set_window_state/get_window.
findings.repro_idea: await tab.maximize(); await tab.set_window_size(200,100,900,700); _, b = await tab.get_window(); assert (b.left,b.top,b.width,b.height) == (200,100,900,700)  # fails. Fix: if the current state is not normal, first send Bounds(window_state=NORMAL) with no geometry, then send the geometry.
findings.evidence: probe10.py headless: 'C set_window_size(200,100,900,700) after maximize: state=normal l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720', and the same after minimize and after fullscreen. probe3.py: '[set_window_size(10,20,900,700) while max] OK' -> 'after size2: state=NORMAL l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720'.

findings.title: minimize()/maximize()/fullscreen() first move and resize the window to 0,0 1280x720, losing the user's restore geometry
findings.bug_class: unintended side effect (default args in internal call)
findings.scenario: await tab.set_window_size(100, 50, 800, 600); await tab.maximize(). For any non-normal target state the code first calls `await self.set_window_state(state='normal')` with the default left=0, top=0, width=1280, height=720. On a normal window that call resizes and moves it to 0,0 1280x720 before maximizing. When the window is restored later (a plain Browser.setWindowBounds(windowState=normal), the user un-maximizing in headful mode, or any restore), it comes back at 0,0 1280x720 instead of 100,50 800x600. A raw CDP maximize keeps the geometry. In headful mode the window also visibly jumps and resizes before every minimize, maximize or fullscreen.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test covers any window-state method.
findings.repro_idea: set_window_size(100,50,800,600); maximize(); send Browser.setWindowBounds(wid, Bounds(window_state=NORMAL)); get_window() shows 0,0,1280,720. A control run with a raw maximize instead of tab.maximize() restores to 100,50,800,600. Fix: restore with Bounds(window_state=NORMAL) and no geometry.
findings.evidence: probe10.py headless: 'A sized: l=100 t=50 w=800 h=600' -> 'A maximized' -> 'A plain restore (no bounds): state=normal l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720', versus the control 'B raw maximize' -> 'B plain restore: state=normal l=100 t=50 w=800 h=600'. Under Xvfb in headful mode, 'after max: l=0 t=0 w=1280 h=720' right after 'after size: l=10 t=20 w=800 h=600'.

findings.title: Tab.__call__ passes text and selector to wait_for in swapped positions, so tab(text=...) runs a CSS query and tab(selector=...) runs a text search
findings.scenario: __call__(text, selector, timeout) calls `self.wait_for(text, selector, timeout)`, but the signature is wait_for(selector, text, timeout). So await tab(text='Hello needle') calls wait_for(selector='Hello needle'), and query_selector('Hello needle') never matches. It loops for the whole timeout and raises TimeoutError even though the text is on the page. await tab(selector='#p1') becomes a text search for '#p1'; it only happens to work because DOM.performSearch also tries the query as a CSS selector. Note: __call__ is just past my scope's end; I report it because it is the public entry point into wait_for.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls a Tab instance (await tab(...)) or Tab.wait_for.

findings.title: evaluate() returns None for Infinity, -Infinity, NaN, -0 and BigInt results with the default return_by_value=True
findings.scenario: await tab.evaluate('1/0'), evaluate('Math.max()') (-Infinity), evaluate('NaN'), evaluate('-0') and evaluate('2n**64n') all return None. CDP puts these values in RemoteObject.unserializable_value ('Infinity', 'NaN', '-0', '18446744073709551616n'), and evaluate only reads remote_object.value. The caller cannot tell the result from undefined or null, and a numeric result such as an empty Math.max/min comes back as None. #203 fixed falsy values (0, [], null) but not these.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_evaluate_return_by_value_falsy covers only 0, [] and null; no test evaluates an expression whose result is non-JSON-serializable.
findings.repro_idea: assert await tab.evaluate('1/0') == float('inf'); assert await tab.evaluate('10n') == 10 -> both fail (None). Fix: when value is None and unserializable_value is set, decode it to float('inf'), float('-inf'), float('nan'), -0.0 or int(x[:-1]).
findings.evidence: probe1.py: '[evaluate(1/0)] OK -> None', '[evaluate(NaN)] OK -> None', '[evaluate(-0)] OK -> None', '[evaluate(10n)] OK -> None'. With return_by_value=False the same expressions give 'NaN' and '10', so the value is available but evaluate drops it on the by-value path.

findings.title: find_element_by_text (and so find()) ignores return_enclosing_element; return_enclosing_element=False still returns the parent element
findings.scenario: Tab.find documents return_enclosing_element=False as the way to get the matched node itself instead of its enclosing element, and it forwards the flag to find_element_by_text. find_element_by_text never reads the parameter, and find_elements_by_text always replaces text nodes with their parent (lines 734-740). So await tab.find('x', return_enclosing_element=False) behaves exactly like True: the flag does nothing, and there is no way to get the matched text node.
